critical_steps: Singleton Parseval vectors in A are precisely isometries s with s*s=1.
Diagonal singleton Parseval vectors in A^k are exactly k-tuples of isometries with pairwise orthogonal ranges.
Two orthogonal isometries v,w generate arbitrarily many v^(j-1)w, giving infinite multiplicity.
Without two orthogonal isometries multiplicity is exactly one.
B(l2(N)) has explicit countably many orthogonal isometries s_j e_n=e_(2^(j-1)(2n-1)); the source proof inequality remains valid for every k.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact left Hilbert C*-module inner-product identities and explicitly constructed orthogonal isometries on l2(N).
integrity.unproved_limits: No classification of nontrivial unitary systems or arbitrary modules and no universal trace-based repair is claimed.

limitations: The dichotomy is proved for the trivial one-element unitary system acting on the canonical left Hilbert module of a nonzero unital C*-algebra; it does not classify arbitrary group-like unitary systems.
The theorem-specific counterexample requires a properly infinite coefficient algebra, which is allowed by the primary source.
The known finite-k orthogonal-isometry criterion is a close antecedent; the direct proof independently establishes the infinite-versus-one dichotomy and pinpoints the failed positivity argument.

title: The trivial unitary system has frame multiplicity \(1\) or \(\infty\) according to proper infiniteness
